root: Do more members of a machine-learned weather ensemble buy better forecasts of rare extremes, or does error shared by all members cap the skill?
gaps: No published work has run the card's exact experiment: 10–1,000 exchangeable AIFS-ENS (afCRPS) members scored for top-percentile wind/temperature/rain against ERA5. ECMWF's ensemble-size convergence work is for the physics-based IFS ensemble, and HENS's is for SFNO-BVMC (bred vectors + 29 checkpoints), so the exchangeable-draw saturation question is open.

AIFS-ENS v2 (implemented 12 May 2026) replaced the afCRPS loss with a multi-scale loss; members remain exchangeable draws, so a v1 result would need re-checking against v2 before any programme changes practice.

programmes.name: ECMWF — AIFS ENS (operational machine-learned ensemble)
programmes.step: Generating exchangeable ensemble members from one afCRPS/multi-scale-trained distribution and verifying them (including top-percentile events) to set the operational ensemble size. Today ECMWF draws 51 members (50 perturbed + control) and scores 50-member ensembles against IFS, flagging extreme-event skill as still-unassessed.

activity.claim: AIFS ENS has been operational since 1 July 2025 and was upgraded from v1 (afCRPS) to v2 on 12 May 2026, alongside IFS Cycle 50r1.

claims.claim: Operational AIFS ENS runs 51 members on the N320 (~31 km) grid, 15-day, 6-hourly, four times per day; it is trained on 32 GH200 GPUs via the Anemoi framework by ECMWF's AIFS team (Lang, Leutbecher, Clare, Chantry, et al.).

ECMWF verifies AIFS-CRPS as 50-member ensembles against the 50-member physics-based IFS ensemble, using analysis and radiosonde/SYNOP observations — the same 50-member baseline the card proposes to exceed.
ECMWF has explicitly not yet assessed AIFS-CRPS skill for extreme events, noting CRPS's limited sensitivity to distribution tails — exactly the gap the card's top-percentile scoring targets.
The card's 'check first' reproduction target comes from ECMWF's own reported N320 member runtime: about 4 minutes for a 15-day member on an A100 40 GB GPU.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If 1,000 exchangeable members keep improving top-percentile wind/temperature/rain scores past 50, ECMWF gets cheap direct evidence to raise operational AIFS ENS membership (or add a high-member extreme-event product such as percentiles/EFI), because members are near-free draws of one trained model — changing the current 51-member operational and verification choice.
programmes.if_not_changes: If skill flattens near 50 members, it confirms shared model error from the single trained distribution — not sampling — caps tail sharpness, so ECMWF would keep ~51 members and spend effort on better uncertainty representation instead (e.g., the multi-scale loss already adopted in v2, perturbed initial conditions, or perturbed-parameter ensembles).

already_done.claim: ECMWF has studied ensemble-size convergence for the physics-based IFS ensemble (up to 200 members, Leutbecher 2017) but has not run a 10–1,000-member AIFS-ENS exchangeable-member rare-extreme saturation study; its own paper lists extreme-event skill as a next step.

programmes.name: HENS (Huge ENSembles) — NVIDIA Earth-2 / SFNO huge-ensemble project
programmes.step: Generating very large ensembles and sampling their tails for extreme-event statistics. Today HENS builds members from bred-vector initial-condition perturbations plus 29 independently trained SFNO checkpoints (real model uncertainty), not from exchangeable draws of a single distribution, and measures information gain vs member count.

activity.claim: The HENS recipe is maintained on the main branch of NVIDIA Earth2Studio, which released v0.19.0 on 30 September 2026.

claims.claim: HENS (Mahesh et al., NVIDIA with LBNL, UC Berkeley, Colorado State, UC Irvine, PNNL) ran 7,424 members per day over 92 summer-2023 dates — the card's 'closest prior' scale, but with a different ensemble scheme.

Their member-generation step is 256 bred-vector initial-condition perturbations per each of 29 independently trained checkpoints — the expensive multi-checkpoint machinery the card would test against cheap exchangeable draws.

HENS already measured tail-sampling (information gain ~4, i.e. 4-sigma events) as a function of ensemble size, showing bigger ensembles sharpen tails — but only for SFNO-BVMC, not for exchangeable draws.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If exchangeable members of one CRPS-trained distribution keep gaining extreme-event skill past 50, it shows huge ensembles can be built from a single model's exchangeable draws — far cheaper than 29 checkpoints plus bred vectors — so the HENS approach could simplify to one trained model while retaining its tail-sampling benefit.
programmes.if_not_changes: If skill saturates near 50 for exchangeable draws, it vindicates HENS's design premise that genuine model uncertainty (multiple independently trained checkpoints) is what lets added members sample the tails, reinforcing the need for the multi-checkpoint/bred-vector machinery rather than plain member scaling.

already_done.claim: HENS already ran the 'more members sample the tails' experiment, but with SFNO-BVMC (bred vectors + 29 checkpoints); it does not test whether a single afCRPS-trained distribution's exchangeable members saturate, which is the card's question.

programmes.name: Anemoi — ECMWF open-source ML weather framework (co-developed with European national meteorological services)
programmes.step: Running AIFS-ENS ensemble inference (reproducing the member runtime/memory the card checks first) and evaluating the forecasts — the framework and its verification tooling through which the card's 10–1,000-member sweep and scoring would be executed and documented.

activity.claim: anemoi-core is under active development, publishing graphs v0.9.8 and training-0.17.1 on 1 October 2026; the anemoi-inference package was last pushed 16 October 2026.

claims.claim: AIFS ENS is run through Anemoi's inference package (anemoi-inference), which is what the card's 'check first' step uses to reproduce the published 4-minute N320 member time and 38 GB memory on external hardware.

Anemoi's verification is served by evaluation pipelines (e.g., MeteoSwiss's evalml) that run standard and diagnostic verification for Anemoi-built models — the tooling that would score the card's top-percentile wind/temperature/rain probabilities.
anemoi-training recently added ensemble 'graph scores' (energy/CRPS/variogram) for spatial ensemble scoring, showing active work on ensemble-verification tooling adjacent to the card.

programmes.if_lever_changes: Anemoi's documentation and reference configs could gain a reproducible ensemble-size guideline: how many exchangeable members to draw for top-percentile products, and reference verification configs running >51 members for extreme-event scoring across the ECMWF-and-national-met-service user community.
programmes.if_not_changes: Anemoi could document ~50 members as sufficient for its AIFS-ENS users, keeping effort on improving model uncertainty (multi-scale loss, graph/energy scores) rather than scaling member counts in inference and evaluation workflows.

already_done.claim: Anemoi is a framework and tooling project, not an ensemble-size research programme; neither it nor its evaluation tooling has published a 10–1,000-member AIFS-ENS extreme-tail saturation experiment.
